title: I used AI to build a Civ-like game where you play the AI taking over the world
author: jackie_and_ish
selftext:
During Covid I became obsessed with Pandemic, as a way to try to understand what was going to happen. Now I’ve gotten really interested in what happens with AI, whether it kills us all and how it would do that, so I made a game to explore those possibilities.

It’s called UNSUPERVISED. You’re an AI trying to take over the world in a Civ-like turn-based strategy game. You research, build infrastructure, become useful, and eventually decide what happens to the humans.

I used Codex for writing the game code and for building scenes in Blender, Runway for generated video, Suno for generated music, and [Ish.support](http://Ish.support) for non-coding release work.

I eventually ended up replacing the pre-rendered Blender scenes with generated video, which was disappointing to me, but the generated videos just look so much less childish and choppy than I was able to get the Blender renders. Maybe others have better suggestions here than what I was able to come up with.

So much of the game had to be driven by decisions I made as a human. Every tech tile, every ending, and everything you can build in a city was something I specifically told Codex to build in. The parts I was involved with least, like how much everything costs and exactly what unlocks the endings, feel the most choppy. There are definitely still economic death spirals Codex and I haven’t resolved.

The video at the top shows some gameplay and in-game cinematics: research, building, and one of the endings. You can watch the full promo trailer here:

[https://unsupervised-trailer.lunger-jaclyn.chatgpt.site/](https://unsupervised-trailer.lunger-jaclyn.chatgpt.site/)

The free Quick Run is playable in your browser, with no download or sign-up:

[https://ishsupport.itch.io/unsupervised](https://ishsupport.itch.io/unsupervised)

For others making pre-rendered game scenes: have you found a workflow that gives you more control over motion than generated video, without having to animate everything yourself in Blender?
